case_name: Krishan Lal Praveen Kumar and Others v State of Rajasthan and Others
petitioner: Krishan Lal Praveen Kumar and Others
facts: The petitioners seek to question the validity of the Rajasthan Wheat (Export Control) Order, 1981 and that of a notification issued under the Rajasthan Trade Articles (Licencing and Control) Order, 1980.

The Rajasthan Wheat (Export Control) Order purports to prohibit the export of wheat from any place within the State of Rajasthan to any place outside the state except under and in accordance with a permit issued by the State Government or any officer authorised by the State Government in that behalf.
It was also submitted that there was an infringement of the fundamental right guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.

The Notification banning a dealer from possessing more than 200 quintals of wheat at any one time, issued u/cl. 18 of the Rajasthan Trade Articles (Licencing and Control) Order, 1980, was questioned on the ground that it infringed the fundamental right guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.

It was also urged that the officers of the State of Rajasthan were misinterpreting the notification and preventing the dealers from purchasing any wheat in the course of a day if at some point of time in the course of the day the dealer was in possession of 200 quintals though, later in the day the quantity in his possession might have gone far below 200 quintals as a result of the transactions of the day.

The aim and object of the Control Order is apparent. It is obviously to conserve the wheat produced in the State of Rajasthan for effective distribution to the people of the State who need them, at reasonable price and to prevent the skyrocketing of the price of wheat within the State of Rajasthan.

It was also submitted that the officers of the State of Rajasthan were misinterpreting the notification and preventing the dealers from purchasing any wheat in the course of a day if at some point of time in the course of the day the dealer was in possession of 200 quintals though, later in the day the quantity in his possession might have gone far below 200 quintals as a result of the transactions of the day.
The Notification merely fixes 'a maximum limit of 200 quintals of wheat to be possessed by a dealer at any one time.'
All that is necessary is that he should not have in his possession at any one time more than 200 quintals.
issues: What it does is to regulate the export of wheat by prohibiting it except under and in accordance with a permit issued by the State Government.
It was also submitted that there was an infringement of the fundamental right guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.

The Notification banning a dealer from possessing more than 200 quintals of wheat at any one time, issued u/cl. 18 of the Rajasthan Trade Articles (Licencing and Control) Order, 1980, was questioned on the ground that it infringed the fundamental right guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.

Whether the Rajasthan Wheat (Export Control) Order, 1981 is an Order which regulates the transport, distribution, disposal of an essential commodity, clearly falling within and authorised by cl. (d) of S. 3(2) of the Essential Commodities Act.
petitioner_arguments: The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners was that the Control Order banned the export of wheat from a place within the State of Rajasthan to a place outside the State of Rajasthan and, therefore, it contravened the provisions of the Constitution which guaranteed freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India.

According to the learned counsel it might be open to Parliament to make a law banning such export from one State to other States but it could not be done by the State Government in the exercise of a delegated power under the Essential Commodities Act.
It was also submitted that there was an infringement of the fundamental right guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
Reliance was placed on a decision of this Court in Automobile Transport (Rajasthan) Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan [1962 Indlaw SC 203].
In any case it was argued that the Control Order was not authorised by the terms of the Essential Commodities Act.

It was also urged that the officers of the State of Rajasthan were misinterpreting the notification and preventing the dealers from purchasing any wheat in the course of a day if at some point of time in the course of the day the dealer was in possession of 200 quintals though, later in the day the quantity in his possession might have gone far below 200 quintals as a result of the transactions of the day.
respondent_arguments: The submission of the learned counsel for the respondents was that the Control Order regulates the export of wheat by prohibiting it except under and in accordance with a permit issued by the State Government.
It was also submitted that there was no infringement of the fundamental right guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
The Notification merely fixes 'a maximum limit of 200 quintals of wheat to be possessed by a dealer at any one time.'
All that is necessary is that he should not have in his possession at any one time more than 200 quintals.
court_reasoning: What it does is to regulate the export of wheat by prohibiting it except under and in accordance with a permit issued by the State Government.

The aim and object of the Control Order is apparent. It is obviously to conserve the wheat produced in the State of Rajasthan for effective distribution to the people of the State who need them, at reasonable price and to prevent the skyrocketing of the price of wheat within the State of Rajasthan.

In our view the Rajasthan Wheat (Export Control) Order 1981 is an Order which regulates the transport, distribution, disposal of an essential commodity, clearly falling within and authorised by cl. (d) of S. 3(2) of the Essential Commodities Act.
The Notification merely fixes 'a maximum limit of 200 quintals of wheat to be possessed by a dealer at any one time.'
All that is necessary is that he should not have in his possession at any one time more than 200 quintals.
